Dear Mr. Sarly,

I forward herewith for your information

the Municipal Police of a communist named Hauh

Dah Yoong(大榮) Rubber Factory, 1 Chining Road.
The accused appeared on remand before the
Second Branch of the Kiangsu High Court on June 13
and was ordered to be handed over to the Chinese
Authorities.

Yours sincerely,

French Police Headquarters.

Proceedings
Mr. Wong: During the remand police found no further
evidence preferred against the accused.
Laung Pau, Rep. of P.S.B.:— Acting on information received
from Loo-wing & Shanghai Garrison Commander in an official letter
(produced) that one named Kau Ching Laung was a communist, on the
5th inst, this man surrendered himself to us, and implicated this
accused and two others as being members of communist party. On the
last hearing, when the accused was questioned in the open Court, he
admitted that he has joined the Labourer Union of Loo Tung Che
(Eastern Shanghai Division) under the control of Chinese settlement.
I ask the Court to hand this accused over to the Public Safety
Bureau for trial.
Accused:— I am not a communist. The man Kau Ching Laung,
who has grudge against me made false implication.
Mr. Wong:— This case was remanded to enable P.S.B. to produce
further evidence and a despatch, but recently, the P.S.B

Subject (in full) Execution of Shanghai Special District Court Warrant No.2760.

Made by F.S. Makaroff Forwarded by J.Blu A.

In accordance with the instructions contained in Warrant
No.2760 issued by the Shanghai Special District Court at the
request of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau for the arrest of
three persons named Zau Kwei Ling(曹桂林), Ting Eu Khaung
(丁厚康) and Hauh Kyi(霍機) working at the Dah Yoong(大用)
Rubber Factory, No.1 Chining Road, members of the Special Branch,
accompanied by detectives from Yulin Road Station and represen-
tatives of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau, visited the above
address at 8 a.m. June 7, 1934.
From enquiries made at the factory, it was ascertained that
the first two named Zau Kwei Ling and Ting Eu Khaung had failed
to report for work since 6.6.34. The third named person was
arrested while at work in the factory. He was identified by
Kau Kyung Sung(高敬生或高金生), a converted communist who was
arrested by the Public Safety Bureau in Chinese controlled
territory on 5.6.34.
Hauh Kyi, on being questioned as to the whereabouts of the
other two wanted persons, stated that he did not know their
addresses. The management of the factory was also unable to
furnish the police with any information regarding the two
absconded persons.
A search of the room occupied by Hauh Kyi(霍機) at No.21
Yoh Hwa Faung(月華坊), Ward Road, failed to reveal anything
of an incriminating nature.
The representatives of the Bureau of Public Safety upon
being asked if they desired a watch kept at the factory for the
other two persons stated that they did not want any further action
to be taken at present.
